note: METHOD. One background script (triage.py) searched all 87 composers: MusicBrainz (batched artist search on name and dates, then work?artist=<mbid>&inc=recording-rels), Deezer (album and track search), and Apple's composerTerm song search for every composer without a Deezer or MusicBrainz hit; a second Apple pass covered nine composers whose Deezer 'hits' were namesakes (Cima, Cobb, Coleman, Colombi, Saint-Germain, Dupuits, Flackton, Guerini, Herwich) and twelve more for composers with Deezer or MusicBrainz hits. Albums were confirmed with Deezer track lists and Apple lookups; IMSLP work pages came through api.php. 7 WebSearch and 1 successful WebFetch (MusicWeb); Presto, Alibris, Gramophone and Linn refused WebFetch. All lookups returned (no FetchError left). SCOPE CALLS. (1) Prints that name flutes before violins (Hasse Op. 2, Fesch Opp. 7 and 12, Croes Op. 5, Gautier's suites) are kept as two violins and continuo with the flute as alternative, as the census files them; several recordings are flute-led (Laurence Dean, BarrocoTout, Hugo Reyne), so the owner may prefer to drop them. (2) Hammerschmidt's Erster Fleiß and Hilton's Prelude and Fantasias are one 'set' entry each: the suite numbers on Savall's disc are inconsistent. (3) Viol consorts recorded only by Phillip W. Serna (De Cousu, Duarte's own set) are not counted; Duarte rests on Ensemble PHOENIX. STRING-ORCHESTRA QUESTIONS (skipped, no one-to-a-part recording found): J. C. F. Fischer, Le Journal du Printemps Op. 1 (L'Orfeo Barockorchester, Freiburger Barockorchester); Durante, Concerti per quartetto (EUCO/Aadland, Ensemble Vox Aurae); Festing Opp. 3 and 5 (Festival Strings Lucerne); Gregori Op. 2 (Capriccio Barockorchester). WORTH A SECOND LOOK. Croes: Divertimenti on the Weverbergh/Terra Nova disc (Nos. 12-14) versus Opp. 2 and 4. Furchheim: 'Suite a 5 in B minor' (Düben collection, filed as unspecified instruments) seems to be on the L'Arpa Festante disc; the E-minor trio is matched by key only. Heinichen: the Sans Souci disc (Stradivarius 2015) is oboe and bassoon trios, so only S.254 (Carus 2022) is kept; the Seibel numbers of S.254 and S.256 differ between IMSLP and Wikipedia. Guerrieri: La Sevasca (a 4) and La Lucina are recorded; their parts are unverified. Guignon: BIS has Op. 4 No. 2 in D major in four movements, Audax (Pramsohler) lists a D-minor Op. 4 No. 2 in three. Fesch: the Globe CD's performers and full track list were not seen. Finger's theatre suites and Dumanoir's Allemande et Sarabande (unspecified-instruments pages) were not checked. Duarte No. 4 is only a 'Seconda Parte' track. WEAK 'none found' (namesake-heavy or variant spellings): Cobb, Drew, Hartley, Hayes, Humble, Humphries, Eyre, Frey, Geist, Hager, Hoffer, Freake, Croubelis. Apple's composerTerm results carry no composer field, so tracks on mixed discs could only be attributed by title, key and movement plan. NAMES. 'Comte de Saint Germain' is written 'Saint-Germain, Comte de'. Frederick II, Ghelardi, Hennersdorff and Gillier le jeune keep the input spelling in composers_checked. BY HAND (orchestrating session, 2026-10-17, on the owner's instruction to leave off lesser-known works that raise flags): 4 work(s) the agent kept at low confidence were moved to skipped (reason "doubtful") and parked in data/chamber/curation/parked-low-confidence.json: Duarte: Sinfonia a 5 No. 4; Furchheim: Sonata a 3 in E minor; Gautier: Suite en trio in C major; Hammerschmidt: Neuer Paduanen, Galliarden, Balletten, Courenten und Sarabanden (Erster Fleiß). RECHECK 2026-10-17: 7 works added (Fesch Trio Sonata Op. 7 No. 4; Guerrieri Sonata a 2 'La Lucina'; Hasse Trio Sonatas Op. 2 Nos. 2, 5, 6 and Op. 3 Nos. 2, 3); 24 lines settled as not performed or recorded (Fesch 2, Croes 2, Fischer 6, Guerrieri 1, Hasse 3, Heinichen 5, Finger 3, Franchi 1, Gautier 1); 2 lines set to doubtful: low confidence (Furchheim Sonata a 5 in A minor; Guerrieri 'La Sevesca', a 4); 0 still not checked.
